answer: The premise is incorrect. node2vec does not use convolutional filters, and it does not replace random walks with them. It relies on random walks. Its key idea is a second-order, biased random walk controlled by two parameters: p (return parameter) and q (in-out parameter). These walks interpolate between breadth-first-search-like exploration (local, structural-equivalence neighborhoods) and depth-first-search-like exploration (broader, homophily-style neighborhoods). The generated walk sequences are treated as sentences and fed to a skip-gram model (word2vec-style) to learn node embeddings. Convolutional filters belong to a different family of methods, such as graph convolutional networks (GCNs), which aggregate neighbor features through learned convolutions rather than sampling walks.
confidence_reasoning: I am highly confident of node2vec's random-walk design with p and q parameters and skip-gram training, and that it does not use convolutional filters, though I am not certifying every detail of the wording.
